text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The return of refugees and displaced people to Eastern Slavonia will start in two weeks' time
- Croatia's natality figures: More babies are born and less abortions are carried out. 1995-1996
- A number of economic agreements with Malaysia seen soon
- Consistent figher for the equality of Croats in Bosnia, Mate Boban who died on Monday
- Are the armies of Poland, Czech Republic and Hungary at all ready for NATO?
- Croatia's GNP still 30 percent lower than in 1989, this according to the UN's social and economic council (ECOSOC) publication
- The financing of the Dayton vision of Bosnia - How the Bosnian federation paid the 3.8 million dollars, last year's debt of the Serb Republic (column)
- Students most interested in studies of economics and law at universities across Croatia
- Bavarian banks grant a 3.5 million German mark loan for the reconstruction of Ludbreg's Bacani Manor and its art restoration centre
- Private dairy group Lura buys the first 850 of 10,000 heifers to help its milk producers, who cooperate with Dukat, Sirela and Zadarska Mljekara dairies

- After the Mars stint is complete I might even nip down to Croatia, says Dr. Jacob Matijevic, the constructor of the Sojourner, the vehicle that has been sent to analyse the surface of Mars, speaking of his Croatian origins
- The semi-presidential election system is to remain in force, says the president's advisor Smiljko Sagolj in an interview -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
